Skin involvement is more variable and may present as ulcerations, frank pyoderma gangrenosum, or severe cystic acne (Fig. 1). Standard laboratory findings typically reflect systemic inflammation but are otherwise non-diagnostic; however elevated production of interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor (TNFα) in peripheral blood leukocytes has been reported in more recent literature [20-22]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a-left, a-right, b-left, b-right). a-left: Sagittal T2-weighted MRI of left knee in PAPA syndrome article with captioned extensive synovitis and subcortical marrow edema, matching in-text inflammatory arthropathy with synovitis and marrow edema. a-right: Transverse T2-weighted MRI of same left knee showing captioned inflammatory process with synovitis and marrow involvement in PAPA pyoarthritis. b-left: Clinical photo of swollen left knee captioned as pyoarthritis in PAPA syndrome case report with in-text left knee arthritis triggered by low-impact trauma. b-right: Clinical photo of inflamed right ankle captioned as pyoarthritis manifestation in same PAPA patient, with in-text new episode of arthritis in right ankle due to trauma.
panels.attribution_text: Fernandes et al. Clinical and Genetic Findings of the First Report of PAPA Syndrome in Brazil.. Case reports in immunology 2021. doi:10.1155/2021/6660937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Magnetic resonance imaging of the left knee. Sagittal plane (left); transverse plane (right), T2-weighted contrast. Presence of an extraarticular infiltrative process with involvement of the subcutaneous tissue and epidermis; inflammatory infiltration of adjacent muscle tissue, without evident collections; small foci of inflammatory edema affecting the subcortical bone marrow; extensive synovitis in the patellar recess and intraarticular involvement. In the transverse plane, there is an increase in the inflammatory process, with volumetric impingement of the popliteus neurovascular bundle. (b) Clinical characteristics of the pyoarthritis. Sequelae with increased left knee volume (left); the inflammatory process in the right ankle caused by trauma from the buckle on footwear (right).
in_text_mentions: Of note, a magnetic resonance imaging of the left knee (Figure 1(a)) showed significant inflammatory arthropathy, with joint effusion associated with diffuse synovitis; extension of the inflammatory process into the periarticular soft parts affecting the popliteus and quadriceps muscle; extrusion of the medial meniscus; and small foci of inflammatory edema affecting the subcortical bone marrow of the trochlear sulcus and the medial femoral condyle, which may have corresponded, according to the radiological report, to the focus of incipient osteomyelitis.

bsequently episodes of left knee arthritis triggered by low-impact local trauma and a new episode of arthritis, this one in the right ankle, due to trauma secondary to the use of inadequate footwear (Figure 1(b)). In these episodes, the response to treatment with prednisone 1 mg/kg over 3 weeks was satisfactory, followed by gradual withdrawal. However, no specific measure could be accessed to infer the impact of the nonpreventive treatment with anti-IL1, as suggested in the literature.
